query: Consider the following context: Constituent phases and their corresponding phase transformations are important in developing alloys. In that context, which method can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The method of composition design and control of cooling rates can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs), as it influences the formation and stability of constituent phases.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA with a disordered face-centered cubic (FCC) structure
generation.intervention: Control of cooling rates during solidification, with a key parameter of cooling rate range from 10 K/s to 100 K/s
generation.conditions: Solidification under atmospheric pressure and without external fields
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary misorientation and lattice distortion
generation.mechanism: Thermodynamic and kinetic control of nucleation and growth of phases, influenced by cooling rate and composition
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in the volume fraction of the ordered B2 phase relative to the disordered FCC phase, as measured by X-ray diffraction, when the cooling rate is increased from 10 K/s to 100 K/s
generation.baseline: As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA with a cooling rate of 10 K/s
generation.boundary: Cooling rates outside the range of 10 K/s to 100 K/s
generation.uncertainty: The actual outcome may be influenced by factors such as composition variations, impurities, and experimental errors, which could affect the accuracy of the prediction

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of cooling rates during solidification of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA, with characterization of phase evolution using X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy
measurements: Volume fraction of ordered B2 phase
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured increase in volume fraction of the ordered B2 phase is less than 10% when the cooling rate is increased from 10 K/s to 100 K/s, the hypothesis is falsified
